title: The Bundle of Sticks

sentences.text: Three cooks in a busy kitchen argued from morning until noon.
One wanted more salt. One wanted more time. One wanted the others to stay out of the way.
Orders piled up, and a pot boiled over because nobody was watching it together.
Their teacher did not shout. The teacher handed each cook a single dry stick.
Break it, the teacher said. Each stick snapped with an easy crack.
Then the teacher tied three sticks into a tight bundle and passed the bundle around.
Each cook tried. Faces reddened. The bundle would not break.
The sticks did not become a new kind of wood, the teacher said. They became harder to snap because they were working as one.
The cooks looked at the spilled pot and at the waiting order tickets.
They split the jobs: one watched the boil, one seasoned at the end, and one plated the food.
The next hour was not perfectly calm, but the food left the kitchen hot and on time.
A single stick had been a quick snap. The bundle had been a lesson they could feel in their hands.
After the meal service, they hung the bundle on a hook where everyone could see it.
The argument was not magically gone. They still had different ideas about salt and timing.
They had learned that different ideas do not help until someone holds them together.

questions.prompt: What is this story mostly about?

choices.text: Working together makes the group harder to break apart
A pot that should never be watched
A teacher who wants the kitchen to close
Three cooks who all want the same job

questions.explanation: One stick snaps, but the bundle does not. The cooks then split the jobs and get the food out on time. Staying together is the main idea.

questions.prompt: What happens to each single stick?

choices.text: It bends and then sprouts leaves
It snaps with an easy crack
It is too strong for anyone to break
It is thrown into the boiling pot

questions.explanation: The teacher asks each cook to break one stick, and each stick snaps easily. The bundle is the thing that will not break.

questions.prompt: In this story, a bundle is what?

choices.text: A single stick before it snaps
The list of order tickets
Things tied together into one group
A pot that has boiled over

questions.explanation: The teacher ties three sticks into a tight bundle. From that action, a bundle means things fastened together as one.

questions.prompt: Why do the cooks hang the bundle on a hook?

choices.text: Because the sticks are now too heavy to hold
So customers can buy the sticks
Because the teacher told them to hide it
So the lesson stays visible while they work

questions.explanation: The story does not say the hook is for storage alone. They hang the bundle where everyone can see it, after learning the lesson with their hands. A reader can figure out that it is a reminder.

questions.prompt: What does the teacher do first?

choices.text: Hands each cook a single stick
Ties three sticks into a bundle
Watches them split the cooking jobs
Sees the bundle hung on a hook

questions.explanation: The single sticks come before the bundle. Splitting the jobs and hanging the bundle happen after the cooks feel the difference.

attribution: A retelling of a public-domain fable by Aesop. The wording is original.
